bindings.label: Patient presented with tension-like headaches for several months

Male veteran in his 40s with a history of posttraumatic stress disorder, traumatic brain injury, and chronic headaches; had undergone tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy in childhood; no sinonasal symptoms, radiation exposure, or trauma.
The headaches were unrelieved by medical treatment.
Head and neck examination including flexible nasopharyngolaryngoscopy showed bilateral fullness of the nasopharynx, with submucosal lesions appearing to be within the torus tubarii.
MRI shows bilateral nasopharyngeal lesions with restricted diffusion
Endoscopy reveals enlarged cystic torus tubarius with purulence after biopsy
Pathology demonstrates benign respiratory mucosa with reactive lymphoid hyperplasia and mild chronic inflammation
Patient has infectious/inflammatory nasopharyngeal lesion caused by Staphylococcus lugdunensis
Patient has an infected nasopharyngeal cyst/abscess caused by Staphylococcus lugdunensis
